results.snippet: Modern LLM-driven text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) systems produce synthetic speech that differs from the generators represented in many legacy spoofing benchmarks. results.title: Calibration Collapse Under Sycophancy Fine-Tuning: How Reward Hacking Breaks Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
results.snippet: Modern large language models (LLMs) are increasingly fine-tuned via reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) or related reward optimisation schemes. While such procedures improve perceived helpfulness, we investigate whether sycophantic reward signals degrade calibration -- a property essential for reliable uncertainty quantification. We fine-tune Qwen3-8B under three regimes: no fine-tuning (base), neutral supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on TriviaQA, and sycophancy-inducing Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) that rewards agreement with planted wrong answers. results.title: Interpretable Preferences via Multi-Objective Reward Modeling and Mixture-of-Experts
results.snippet: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as the primary method for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. The RLHF process typically starts by training a reward model (RM) using human preference data. Conventional RMs are trained on pairwise responses to the same user request, with relative ratings indicating which response humans prefer. The trained RM serves as a proxy for human preferences. However, due to the black-box nature of RMs, their outputs lack interpretability, as humans cannot intuitively understand why an RM thinks a response is good…

results.snippet: Kinetic equations play a major rule in modeling large systems of interacting particles. Recently the legacy of classical kinetic theory found novel applications in socio-economic and life sciences, where processes characterized by large groups of agents exhibit spontaneous emergence of social structures. Well-known examples are the formation of clusters in opinion dynamics, the appearance of inequalities in wealth distributions, flocking and milling behaviors in swarming models, synchronization phenomena in biological systems and lane formation in pedestrian traffic. # 价值对齐与可扩展监督（含校准与不确定性量化）前沿调研报告（2024-2026）

**日期**：2026-11-08（UTC）  
**领域**：AI Safety / Value Alignment / Scalable Oversight / Calibration & Uncertainty Quantification  
**检索源数量**：31 条（其中高度相关 9 条：[5][7][13][21][22][23][24][27][30]）

---

## 1. 进展与热点

### 1.1 一句话增量判断
2024-2026 年，**奖励黑客导致校准崩溃**被首次严格量化实证，**多目标奖励建模**与**信息论奖励建模**成为缓解对齐偏移的两条主流技术路线，**可扩展监督基准**与**多语言价值对齐共享任务**开始形成标准化评测体系。

### 1.2 关键进展条目（按时间倒序）

| 进展 | 时间 | 机构/作者 | 增量贡献 | 证据等级 | 热度证据 | 权威证据 | 关注度 | 推荐度 | 来源 |
|------|------|-----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|--------|--------|------|

| **PlurVA-LLM-2026 Shared Task Track-1** | 2026-09 | 共享任务组织方 | 首个面向多语言、多元价值对齐的基准任务，引入阈值校准机制评测模型在多元文化语境下的对齐稳定性 | B | > 待核实 | 共享任务论文（AAMAS/COLING 等会议配套） | 中 — 新基准，社区关注度上升中 | ★★★★☆ 推荐：可扩展监督评测标准化的重要里程碑 | [21] |

| **SORT-AI: Projection-Based Framework for Alignment Stability** | 2025-12 | SSRN / Preprints.org | 提出投影结构框架，统一对齐稳定性分析、漂移检测与可扩展监督，提供理论可验证的监控指标 | C (working paper) | > 待核实 | SSRN 工作论文 + 预印本平台 | 低-中 — 理论框架类，工程落地验证尚少 | ★★★☆☆ 理论参考：为监督系统设计提供结构化思路 | [22][23] |
